questions.question: What is the nature-nurture controversy? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the nature-nurture controversy? [K] / [CO1]
  • It refers to the debate about whether heredity (nature) or environment (nurture) plays the
  • major role in the development of an individual. Hereditarians believe development is mainly
  • influenced by heredity, while environmentalist s believe environment has the greater
  • influence. (two points- 1 mark each)

questions.question: Explain in brief, how the different domains of development are interconnected. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain in brief, how the different domains of development areinterconnected. [K] / [CO1]
  • A child's progress in one domain influences the progress in other domains of development. Good physical
  • health contributes to self-confidence and better social interactions. Physical activities like sports promote
  • teamwork and leadership skills etc.(Explanation – 2 marks and two examples – 2 marks)

questions.question: How do various domains of development influence each other? Discuss with examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• How do various domains of development influence each other? Discuss with examples.
  • [K] / [CO1]
  • The domains of development are interconnected so that a child's progress in one domain
  • influences the progress in other domains of development. Example: Healthy brain
  • development (physical development) aids cognitive functioning. Cognitive development
  • helps in emotional control and social interaction. Language development improves
  • communication and promotes social development. (Explanation – 2 marks and any two
  • examples – 2 marks)

  • whole, possible without growth.(Four points for each growth and development - ½ mark each)

  • nutrition can cause delayed growth and development. (2 marks)

questions.question: Describe the purpose, features, advantages and disadvantages of experimental method. / [CO2] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the purpose, features, advantages and disadvantages of experimental method.
  • [U] / [CO2]
  • Purpose: The experimental method is a method of studying children through experiments
  • conducted in a controlled setting to understand behavio ur, learning, and development. (2½
  • marks)
  • Features: Controlled Setup, Testing Cause and Effect, Groups for Comparison, Repeatable
  • Results. (2½ marks)
  • Advantages: Gives clear and reliable results , Helps find out what causes certain behaviors ,
  • Reduces errors by controlling other factors. (2½ marks)
  • Limitations: Children may act differently in an artificial setting, Some experiments may raise
  • ethical concerns, The results may not always apply to real-life situations. (2½ marks)
  • [10x1 = 10]
